candidate_relations.reason: The CT did show acute interstitial pancreatitis, making this a real component of the clinical picture. However, the benchmark requires complete pancreatic divisum (supported by EUS ductal anomaly and non-opacification of neck/body/tail on ERCP) and pancreatic-pleural fistula (supported by ERCP leak toward diaphragm and amylase-positive transudative pleural effusion). C001 captures only the inflammatory component and misses both the congenital ductal anomaly and the fistulous complication that constitute the final diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Acute interstitial pancreatitis is a component finding on CT but omits the pancreatic divisum (ductal anomaly on EUS) and the pancreatic-pleural fistula (ERCP leak toward diaphragm, amylase-positive pleural effusion), which are the defining elements of the benchmark diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: Benchmark composite diagnosis requires two distinct components: structural anomaly (complete pancreatic divisum) and complication (pancreatic-pleural fistula); single-component candidates will inherently be partial.

EUS finding of 'pancreatic duct anomaly' and ERCP non-opacification of neck/body/tail are the key anchors for pancreatic divisum; amylase-positive pleural effusion with ERCP fistula toward diaphragm anchors the pleural fistula.
